rationale: C14 plausibly supplied a material drafting template: both directives recite the acquisition or donation of a particular tract for addition to an existing federally protected land unit, make a public-interest finding, and proceed to an operative inclusion followed immediately by a metes-and-bounds description. The shared sequence and closely parallel language are more concrete than a generic land-management resemblance. C03 reproduces much of C14's relevant text but has a mismatched title and opening recital, making it a weaker candidate as displayed. C07 uses similar monument-addition machinery but is less closely matched.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS it appears that such lands are suitable for national-forest purposes and that their inclusion within the Cherokee National Forest would be in the public interest
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Whereas it appears that it would be in the public interest to reserve such tract of land as an additional to the said Aztec Ruins National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Both use a specific public-interest recital to justify adding acquired land to an existing protected federal land unit.

shared_material.child_excerpt: NOW, THEREFORE, A tract of land lying in the first Civil District of Polk County...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Now, Therefore... the following-described tract of land in New Mexico is hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Aztec Ruins National Monument: Beginning at a point...
shared_material.explanation: Both move directly from the public-interest finding to inclusion of the tract and its detailed legal description.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Tennessee Valley Authority and the United States Department of Agriculture entered into an agreement providing for the transfer... of certain lands... so reserved as a part of the Cherokee National Forest
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Southwestern Monuments Association... has donated the said tract of land to the United States for addition to such monument
shared_material.explanation: The acquisition mechanism differs, but both recitals establish that a specifically obtained tract is available for incorporation into an existing conservation unit.
